name: Single-Arm Kettlebell Curl (Eccentric-Emphasis)
description: Stand tall holding a kettlebell by the handle in one hand, arm hanging at your side, palm forward. Curl the bell by flexing at the elbow, keeping the upper arm pinned to your ribs and the shoulder packed down — no swinging the elbow forward. Lower slowly to a full stretch at the bottom. Unlike a dumbbell, the bell's mass hangs below and behind the handle, so the bottom of the rep stays loaded where a dumbbell goes slack; that stretched position is the point of doing it with a bell. Eccentric-emphasis variant: if the bell is too heavy to curl cleanly, assist the way up with a hip pop or the free hand, then lower it slowly with the working arm alone — the lowering is the work. Lead with the weaker arm and match the stronger arm to it.
